The ERP keeps customers, stock and invoicing: Business Central remains your system of record. We hold the order guide for every account, priced your way, plus a copy of every order made in our app.

Emailed orders can stay with Business Central's agent: Customers who email an order or send a PDF can carry on that way, and your staff keep approving the agent's replies. Our app is there for kitchens where talking comes easier than writing. We give no number to an order phoned to you; the app numbers only what comes through it.

A partner's web portal can stay too: Business Central has no customer ordering portal of its own; partners sell them as add-on apps. Accounts already using one can carry on. Two ways in for two kinds of kitchen is fine.

@graph.name: Do we need a Business Central alternative to add voice ordering?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Business Central keeps its job as your ERP, and its agent can keep handling emailed orders. What we add is a check at the kitchen's end, made before anything reaches you. Start with the customers who phone you most.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than Business Central?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only at one job: letting the kitchen catch its own mistakes before you receive the order. The rest is Business Central's work, which is why our app sits beside it.

@graph.name: Doesn't Business Central's AI agent already take orders?

acceptedAnswer.text: It does, from email. It reads a customer's message and any PDF or photo, matches the items, prepares a quote first, and asks your staff to approve each reply before it goes. Our app works earlier: a chef says what is needed and fixes each line before it is sent. Neither one makes a wrong order impossible. The difference is who checks it, and when.

@graph.name: Can kitchens use Business Central's own mobile app?

acceptedAnswer.text: That app was made for your licensed staff: they sign in with their Business Central user name to review data, edit records and email quotes. It is not an app for your customers to order in. Voice add-ons for Business Central exist too: the one we found is built for drive-thru lanes and self-service kiosks, and partners can build custom ones. Ours sits with the kitchen: the chef talks each order through and corrects any line before it reaches you.

@graph.name: Does any link join VoiceOrder Solutions and Business Central?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. They are sold separately, nothing links them out of the box, and neither of us offers support for the other side. Over EDI or the API, the app can pass an order straight in with no retyping, if the way Business Central is set up for you allows it; we check that together in the demo. Emailed orders hold lines the kitchen has already approved, and your staff key them in from there instead of from a call.

@graph.name: Will you need a Business Central login from us?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not to get set up. We need no login and install nothing: we work from an export you send us, so your permissions and customizations are left alone. If EDI or API delivery interests you later, we go through what it needs on your side in the demo.

@graph.name: How long does setup take, and is pricing published?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setup takes 24 to 48 hours for most distributors. Business Central publishes per-user prices for its plans; we publish none and give every distributor its own quote. A Business Central replacement, or any Business Central alternative, means moving every customer, item and ledger to a new system. Our app moves none of them.

@graph.name: Where do the Business Central details here come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: From Microsoft's Business Central product and pricing pages and its help articles, checked on 9 November 2026: the AI order agent, item tracking, the phone app for staff and the plans, plus a web search for voice tools other companies sell for it. Their prices are published there, so we leave the figures to them. If something here no longer holds, write to us and the page gets corrected.
